notes: Primary ask: Dedicated capacity for payment-critical LLM workloads (checkout assistant + fraud scoring).
Throughput targets: steady-state ~200 qps (small prompts), burst up to 500 qps; token throughput estimate ~600k tokens/min peak.
Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end generation <= 250ms for 128-token responses; p99 <= 500ms. Horizon emphasizes tail latency for checkout flow.

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask for 2x high-memory GPUs (customer suggested A100/80GB equiv) with autoscale burst to handle promo events. Want sizing guidance from Redwood based on observed POC numbers.
Model preferences: open models preferred (cost) but will accept vendor variants if latency/quality tradeoffs favorable. Want model pinning + rollback plan for Dedicated.

Traffic shaping & priority lanes: must support tenant isolation + per-route quotas. Payment-auth routes must be prioritized (hard lane) to ensure low tail latency. Background reranking/embeddings can be rate-limited and batched aggressively.

Noisy-neighbor controls: Horizon requires per-tenant token quotas, CPU/GPU isolation options, and preemption for lower-priority routes. Interested in Redwood's admission control, queueing policies, and kernel-level isolation (MPS/cgroups) options.
SLA negotiation points: guaranteed baseline throughput (requests/sec) with credits for breaches; clarifying measurement (model-inference vs end-to-end); scheduled maintenance windows and hotfix SLAs.
Observability needs: token-level cost/latency per route, tracing of falling-back-to-smaller-model events, alerting on SLO regressions tied to test prompts.
Security/compliance: VPC + KMS mandatory, logs retention 7 years (legal asked), and export control/data residency restrictions for EU customers. Legal to provide SOC2 addendum wording.
POC plan: phase 1 baseline perf (small prompts, 128t) + noisy neighbor injected traffic; phase 2 routing/priority lanes testing; phase 3 soak test across 48 hours including burst scenarios.
Quotes from calls: 'We cannot have checkout stalls during peak promos' (CTO); 'Need clear definition of what counts as a breach for SLA credits' (Legal).
Open items: define hard vs soft priority lanes, exact quota numbers per route, fallback model set, and commitment on reserved GPU count/cost/term.
